newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar stays in tight range in subdued Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar stays in tight range in subdued Tokyo trade.

text.p: 0619 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar remained in a tight range against the yen by late Tokyo on Thursday as trading energy ebbed ahead of U.S. trade data due later in the day and the June 20-22 Group of Seven (G7) summit in Denver.
The greenback was supported near 113.20 yen after a downside test in early trade on comments from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin ended in failure, dealers said.
Rubin said on Wednesday in Washington it was "very important" that Japan achieve growth led by domestic demand and avoid a sustained increase in its trade surplus.

Following his comments, the dollar dipped as low as 113.27 yen in early trade as the market took his comments to mean that the U.S. government was indeed disturbed by recent rises in Japan's trade surplus, dealers said.

Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus, often the source of bitter rows with the United States, jumped more than 200 percent in May from a year earlier to 738.27 billion yen ($6.53 billion), the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

But U.S. operators, Japanese investors, including life insurers, and public funds were said to be raising their bids to around 113.20 yen. This prevented follow-through sales emerging and kept the greenback's downside limited, dealers said.
They added that market participants remained reluctant to take heavy fresh positions ahead of U.S. international trade data for April due out at 1230 GMT and the G7 summit.
"Trade is very thin ahead of the U.S. trade data and the G7 summit. Speculative accounts have been very quiet so far for that reason," a dealer at a city bank said.
